title: Data Modeling
summary: Treats data modeling as a collaborative design discipline focused on well-formed, high-fidelity representations of organizational facts and relationships.

concepts.title: Purpose and scope
concepts.summary: A data model identifies facts and relationships that must be stored without deciding physical storage or process logic.

concepts.title: Modeling building blocks
concepts.summary: Entities, attributes, identifiers, and relationships form the core vocabulary for communicating a database design.

concepts.title: Well-formed models
concepts.summary: A well-formed model follows notation rules, names every entity, supplies identifiers, records relationships, and avoids ambiguous labels.

concepts.title: High-fidelity models
concepts.summary: A high-fidelity model accurately reflects the real-world context, including relevant relationships, constraints, and exceptions.

concepts.title: Context and exceptions
concepts.summary: Model quality depends on intended use, so designers test edge cases and exceptions rather than assuming the first simple model is sufficient.

concepts.title: Cardinality and modality
concepts.summary: Cardinality describes maximum participation and modality describes whether participation is optional or mandatory.

concepts.title: Generalization and entity types
concepts.summary: Shared facts across related entity types can be generalized into a broader entity while subtype-specific facts remain distinct.

concepts.title: Identifiers and naming
concepts.summary: Identifiers and labels should be stable, meaningful to stakeholders, internally consistent, and unambiguous in context.

concepts.title: Iterative modeling
concepts.summary: Models improve through repeated challenge, testing, integration, and completeness checks with client participation.
